Subject: Collection of Establishment Master Database for EPFIGMS

‘Sir,

The EPFIGMS an internet based grievance management system of EPFO is ready for
launch. This application software is database driven which guides the movement of the
grievances lodged to the offices. to which grievances might pertain. For this purpose updated
establishment master of all the field offices needs to be loaded into the EPFIGMS before its
launch.

Hence you are requested to kindly send updated establishment master of your
Region/Office in the following format /structure provided by the JS Division. The required
information is tabulated below

Sl.No. | Field (s) Description | Example
1. REG_CODE Two character Regional Code DS for Delhi (South)
2. ACC_OF_DLT Three character Office Code CBE for Coimbatore
3. OFFICE The office name Indore for Regional
Office, Indore
4. | EST_CODE EstablishmentCode | 68456
5. EST_EXT | Establishment Extension - A : |
6. EST_NAME Name of the Establishment M/s. ABC India Limited
7 COVER_DT Coverage Date 21/03/1991
8 ADDRESS1 Establishment Address Line 1 44/A Okhla Industrial
Area
9. ADDRESS2 Establishment Address Line 1 Okhla Phase —|
10. CITY City/Town/Place where the Establishmentis | New Delhi
located
DISTRICT Name of the District in which the Delhi South
Establishment is located

PIN Pin code of the area of the Establishment 110020

Offices running legacy application software may be requested to extract the above information
in dbf format and send it. While doing so, they have to populate the REG_CODE and OFFICE
fields by using the ‘replace’ command.“

The Establishment master database of all the offices in your region may kindly be sent
by 05.04.2010 to the claims-epfo@nic.in (P/ mark EPFIGMS database in subject) and
subsequently in CD to the undersigned.

Subject: Posting of technical personnel through NICSI for supporting project implementation –
regarding.
.
Sir,
In order to ensure smooth implementation of the 'Computerization project' the headquarters
office had placed an order with NICSI to provide 2 (two) technical persons to assist your office in the
technical aspects of the project for an initial period of 6 (six) months. NICSI in turn has placed orders on
their empanelled vendors M/s. CyberQ Consulting Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi for providing technical personnel
in respect of your office.
The NICSI vendor M/s. CyberQ Consulting Pvt. Ltd., would be assigning these personnel (at least
one) to your office. These technical personnel would either have reported for duties at your office or
will be shortly assigned to your office. These technical personnel will carry out general system and
database administration functions as well as other technical matters related to Server, UPS, Printers,
networking, etc. and also function as first level trouble shooters. They will also liaison with concerned
vendors and parties to log issues and problems and get them resolved. It may also be ensured that
technical personnel of EPFO are also adequately trained to take over such responsibilities within six
month.
Report on the joining of such technical personnel may be sent to headquarters for record and
necessary action. Attendance record of such personnel should be maintained separately and copy
provided to NICSI vendor on monthly basis for regulating their payments to the individuals concerned.
Encl:-As above.

Subject:
Procedure for empanelment of advocates.
Sir,
You are aware that EPFO has to contest cases before various
judicial/semi judicial fora in connection with the following:-.
Substantial Question(s) of law arising before the Supreme Court/High
Courts in connection with the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and the various
Schemes framed thereunder.
Appeals made before EPF Appellate Tribunal against the orders made
under the Act and the Schemes e.g. under Section 7A of the Act etc.
Actions brought before, the subordinate courts of law and the consumer
courts for denial/deficiencies of service by EPFO.
Other litigations where EPFO is involved.
In order to make the best possible representation in such cases,
EPFO requires to be assisted by a panel of competent advocates.
The panel of advocates shall be recommended by the RPFCs
heading the regions to the Head Office. On the basis of the RPFC's
recommendations the Head Office shall constitute the panel for the
region for a block of two years at a time. While recommending the
names of the advocates for empanelment, the RPFCs shall be
guided by the following factors:-

(a)
Scope
A panel of lawyers shall be required only for handling the
cases pertaining to the Supreme Court, the High Court, the
CAT, the EPFAT, the National Commission and the State
Commissions constituted under the Consumer Protection
Act, 1986. The'proceedings of the Subordinate Courts and
the District Consumer Fora involve mostly questions of fact
and shall be attended to by the local EPFO machinery only.
In cases of special need articulated by the RPFC, a panel for
pOrposes of the subordinate judiciary and the District Fora
may, however, be approved by the Head Office.
(b)
Qualifying practice
Generally 10 years of relevant legal practice shall be
required for Supreme Court, High Court, State Consumer
Dispute Redressal Commission, the National Consumer
Dispute Redressal Commission the Central Administrative
Tribunal and the EPF Appellate Tribunal where questions of
law are frequently involved and hence considerable legal
expertise and experience are required. In rare cases, the
RPFC, may, however, recommend the applications of
talented and promising advocates who though falling short
of the experience criterion, have had an excellent academic
background and are recommended by atleast two eminent
figures in the legal field. Alternatively, his/her suitability
may be decided on the basis of a personal interview by a
committee constituted by the Head Office for the purpose.
In addition, a Central Govt. Standing Counsel or an
Additional Central Govt. Standing Counsel could be engaged
without their formal empanelment for EPFO.
(c)
Size of the Panel
RPFCs shall ensure that the pool of advocates (including the
Central Govt. Standing Counsel and Additional Central Govt.
Standing Counsel) is optimally utilized by a fair distribution
of cases.
â The size of the panel recommended by the RPFCs
should be proportionate to the number of cases
pending with and arising in the region. An upper limit
of the no. of advocates on the panel shall be stated
by the RPFCs.
The RPFCs shall explain the reason behind
recommending re-empanelment of advocates who
were not allotted substantial work in the past.

organisations under his charge to organize and coordinate the meeting. On receipt of the
directions from the Joint Secretary concerned, it will be the responsibility of the Head of Office of

meetings in respect of all the offices/officers of the Ministry of Labour & Employment in that
region including inviting the Heads of other Offices of the Ministry of Labour & Employment or
their representatives located in that region. An illustrative list of field offices of the Ministry of
Labour & Employment has been enclosed at Annexure II of the aforesaid D.O. letter dated

quarterly meeting is convened shall be the Nodal Officer. Whenever a meeting is convened for a

information on the performance of the other regions shall be presented by the Nodal Officer in
the meeting.

mechanism may be devised in consultation with concerned officers so that actions are properly
coordinated as and when a meeting is called by the Joint Secretary concerned or any direction is

Manager.

3. Restart the Thin Client

4. Login to Administrator
5. Create two directories namely TEMP and TMP at the C:Drive.

Environment Variables.

8. TEMP=C:\TEMP
9. TMP=C:\TMP

Subject: -Addition of a new ABP return pertaining to International Workers.

Sir,

| am directed to say that in consequent to the Social Security Agreements initiative taken by
the Ministry of Oversees Indian Affairs, Government of India, EPFO has been identified as the
liaison agency to implement the provisions of the agreement in India and has been authorized
to issue certificate of coverage to the employees of Indian establishments in the countries with
whom agreements have been entered. In order to accommodate the provisions of the bilateral
agreements, enabling provisions have been made in the Schemes and have come into effect from
01-10-2008. At headquarters the International Workers Unit has been setup to look after the
administrative issues and issues relating to implementation policy.

Accordingly, a proforma of new return pertaining to the International Workers in enclosed
herewith at Annexure-l. It has been decided to incorporate proforma in ABP Returns as the 10”
sheet. The information on the International Workers would henceforth be sent along with other ABP
Returns by 5" day of every month as is done at present in other returns. The ABP Returns
consolidated for each month may be sent by e-mail at neomishg@yahoo.com followed by hardcopy
as per the usual practice.

It is reiterated that each Regional Office would indicate in the ABP Returns consolidated
data in upto the Month format i.e the return for the month of September will contain the data for the
period April to September. Similarly the return for the month of December will contain the data for
the period April to December.

This issues with the approval of competent authority..

Siubject:-
Enhancement in the rate of Fixed Medical Allowance, payable to the
serving as well as retired employees of the EPFO for outdoor medical
treatment - regarding.
Sir,
I am directed to convey the approval of the 67 th Executive Committee, held on
4.12.2009;CBT EPF for enhancement of the Fixed Medical Allowance _(FMA) from Rs.600/.p.m.
(Rupees Six hundred only ) to Rs. 1200/- p.m.(Rupees one thousand two hundred only). This
enhancement will be effective from 1 st January, 2009 and subject to the following conditions.
(i)
The enhancement of fixed medical allowance will be available to_serving employees and
pensioners (including family pensioners) of the Employees Provident Fund Organization.
The serving employees of the Organization who are in the Head Office at New Delhi and
Regional / Sub Regional Office at Delhi and at stations which are covered by the Central
Government Health Scheme will not be eligible for Fixed Medical Allowance. As soon as
any employees is covered by Central Government Health Scheme , the fixed medical
allowance admissible to him/ her shall be stopped.
(ii)
If two or more members of family-are working in the EPF Organisation, only one of them
will be eligible for the facility of fixed medical Allowance.

(iii)
In the case of an employee whose wife / husband spouse is an employee of a Government
or any other organization (including private Firm /Office ) he/she will be required to give
an undertaking that his /her spouse is not availing of medical facilities in cash , if any
granted by their respective employees.
(iv)
The Fixed Medical Allowance will be in lieu of the medical facility available for outdoor
treatment under-the Central Services (Medical Attendance) Rules, 1944 as adopted by the
EPF Organisation for its own employees and pensioners
Your faithfully
(V.P. Ramaiah)

Certain references have been received from the Members of the Internal
Audit Teams about the admissibility of the following facilities:
(i) Conveyance Charges for the journeys performed to various ROs
and SROs within the Headquarters.
(ii) Conveyance Charges for the journeys performed from
one Station to the Camp Station.
(iii) Travelling Allowance for visiting the respective Headquarters
Office every month from the Camp Station for the purpose of
admissibility of Transport Allowance in respect of Members
of the Internal Audit Teams.
02.
All the above issues have been examined with reference the prevailing
instructions contained in the FR & SR and as per various clarifications received in
the light of the 6th. Pay Commission recommendations and accordingly the
following clarifications are issued for uniform adoption in respect of all the
Internal Audit Parties:
(i)
The Internal Audit Parties are required to remain at the 'Camp Place only
and as far as possible nearer to the Office Of the Audit. All the ROs and SROs
falling within the Same agglomeration limits to be treated as Headquarters. E.g.
Mumbai - Bandra RO, Thane Ro °and KandiVali RO and SROs under them within
the city of Mumbai. Similarly, Delhi North; Delhi South and SRO within the city
of New Delhi etc. irrespective of the distance between each office. The Rule is

Sir,

I am directed to invite your attention to this office circular letter No. HRMI1/17(01)2009/EO-AO/STY LIST-03/2005/4772-4942 dated 24.04.2009 through
which draft seniority list of Enforcement Officers/Accounts Officers appointed on
regular basis as on 31.03.2005 in the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation was
circulated by this office wherein all the points on which the seniority list of EO/AO
was prepared had been clarified, yet it is reiterated.

2. In response to the above various representation were received by this office.
All these representation have been examined. Replies to the points raised in the
representations received have since been forwarded to the respective Regional P.F.
Commissioners separately for informing the same to the officers concerned.

3: The revised seniority list, after conducting Review DPCs for promotion to the
post of EO/AAO(Now designated as A.O.) on regular basis w.e.f. 04.03.90 onwards
in compliance of judgment dated 05.12.06 passed by Hon’ble CAT Principal Bench,
New Delhi in OA No. 2472/1999 and MA 1124-1125/2005 filed by Shri B.P. Jain &
Others and the judgment dated 15.02.2006 passed by Hon’ble CAT, Bangalore Bench
in OA No. 517 & 664 To 667/2004 filed by Shri N.K. Ranganathan in supersession of
all previous draft seniority lists, which were issued by this office from time to time in
respect of EO/AAO (Now designated as A.O.) appointed between 04.03.90 to
31.03.2005 under three mode of recruitment as prescribed in the Recruitment Rules

1

for the post of EO/AAO(Now designated as A.O.) i.e. Departmental Promotion (DP),
Departmental Competitive Examination (EQ) and Direct Recruitment (DR), is
enclosed for circulation among the officers whose names are included in the list and
who are still in service as on date.

4. In this connection, following points are highlighted for information:-

(i) Seniority has been assigned by considering the cases as per the provisions of
the EPF Staff (Fixation of Seniority) Regulations, 1989 alongwith the guidelines
contained in the Circular Letter No. HRM-III/2(97)/TN dated 21.05.2001.

(ii) | All Departmental Promotion Quota candidates have been placed against the
respective year -wise vacancies pertaining to the DP Quota against which they were
regularized.

(iii) Departmental Promotion Quota candidates have been assigned seniority against
the DP Quota vacancies on the basis of the date as recommended by the DPC/Review
DEC:

(iv) Wherever the date of promotion in respect of two or more officers in the cadre
of EO/AAO (Now designated as A.O.) of different regions were same, the seniority in
such cases has been decided on the basis of their relative seniority in the cadre of
Section Supervisor/Feeder Cadre.

(v) | The name of officials who had been considered for promotion as on 03.03.90 in
compliance of the Judgment of CAT Bangalore Bench in Shri N.K. Ranganathan
case by the Review DPCs of the different Regional Offices, have been reflected in the
addendum to seniority list of EO/AAO as on 03.03.90.

(vi) The rota-quota system consisting of DP, EQ and DR candidates has been
implemented only in the year in which more than one mode of recruitment has taken
place.

(vii) All the Departmental Examination Quota 1.e. (EQ) candidates have been
assigned seniority on the basis of their merit in the result.

(viii) Where more than one candidates have been assigned same ranking/ merit, they
have been placed in the seniority list as per their seniority in the feeder cadre/Section
Supervisor.

(ix) All Direct Recruitment (DR) Quota officials have been assigned seniority
against the financial year in which they have joined in the order of their merit in the
Select List drawn by UPSC.

(x) All Direct Recruitment Quota officials are required to join duty within a
specified time. So, the officials selected under DR quota who have not joined the post
within six months from the date of issue of order have been shown junior in the same
year.

OFFICE MEMORANDUM
Subject : Grant of Dearness Relief to Central Government
pensioners/family pensioners — Revised rate effective
from 1.7.2009.
The undersigned is directed to refer to this Department's OM
NO 42/12/2009-P&PW(G) dated 27th March; 2009 on the subject mentioned
above and to state that the President is pleased to decide that the Dearness
Relief payable to Central Government pensioners shall be enhanced from the
existing rate of 22% to 27% w.e.f. 1 5t July, 2009.
2.
These orders apply to (i) All Civilian Central Government
Pensioners/Family Pensioners (ii) The Armed Forces Pensioners, Civilian .
Pensioners paid out of the Defence Service Estimates, (iii) All India Service
Pensioners (iv)
.Railway . Pensioners and (v). The Burma Civilian
pensioners/family ' pensioners and pensioners/families of displaced
Government pensionerS from Pakistan, who are Indian Nationals but
receiving pension on behalf of Government of Pakistan, who are in receipt of
ad-hoc ex-gratia allowance of Rs. 3500/- p.m. in terms of this Departments
OM' No. 23/1/97-P&PW(B) dated 23.2.1998 read with this Department's OM
No. 23/3/2008-P&PW(B) dated 15.9.2008.
3.
Central Government Employees who had drawn lumpsum
amount on absorption in a PSU/Autonomous body and have become eligible
to restoration of 1/3rd commuted portion of pension as well as revision of the
restored amount in terms of this Department's OM No. 4/59/97-P&PW (D)
dated 14.07.1998 will also be entitled to the payment of DR @ .27% w.e.f.
1.7.2009 on-full pension i.e. the revised pension which the , absorbed
employee would have received on the date of restoration had he not drawn
lumpsum payment on absorption and Dearness Pension subject to fulfilment .2
of the conditions- laid down in 'para 5 of the O.M. dated 1 .4.07.98. In this
connection, instructions contained in this Department's OM No.4/29/99P&PW (D) dated 12.7.2000 refers.
4.
Payment of DR involving a fraction of a rupee shall be rounded off to
the next higher rupee.
5.
Other provisions governing grant of DR in respect of employed family
pensioners and re-employed Central Government Pensioners will be
regulated in accordance with the provisions contained in this Department's
OM No. 45/73/97-P&PW (G) dated 2.7.1999 as amended vide this
Department's OM No. F. No. 38/88/2008-P&PW(G) dated 9th July, 2009.
.
The provisions relating to regulation of DR where pensioner is in receipt of
more than one pension will remain unchanged.

The workshop started with an address by Sri Uttam Prakash, RPFC II, Project
who told about the purpose of the workshop, informing that it was called to discuss
new ideas for improvement of the services in view of the Computerisation Project and
that it was basically a brain storming session to come out with suggestions on
improving services and discuss their implementation strategy.

Sri B K Panda, ACC (IS) then welcomed the participants requesting them to
come out openly with their suggestions. He also informed that a presentation by the
ICICI team was also arranged on payment gateway through website.

Sri Chandramauli Chakraborty, RPFC | informed al! the members about the
rules of the workshop stating that all ideas were welcome and the requested
participants to try to suggest solutions on the problems that come up for discussion
instead of criticizing any idea.

A presentation was made by them. They showed how a payment gateway was
being planned for the ESIC and that the gateway will have all options namely
payment through credit/debit card, net banking and through challan. Such gateway if
provided through the official website of EPFO will provide the willing employers
with an option to pay their dues online. It was decided that M/s ICICI shoutd prepare
a demo with EPFO requirements in mind so that it may be presented before the senior
officers of the Organisation.

After the ICICI team left, Sri S K Suman, RPFC II, Project informed all the
participants about the status of the Project and the future roll out plan. Sri Rajasekhar
Reddy, RPFC II from Hyderabad informed that the Project was running smoothly at
Hyderabad and approximately 1500 claims were being settled per day. The
achievement of the Hyderabad office was applauded by all and it was decided to
upload a news item on the performance of Hyderabad Office on the EPFO website.

Subject: Assessment of penal damages u/s 14B of EPF & MP Act.

Sir,

As you are aware that all belated remittances towards PF dues attract
damages by way of penalty as per provisions laid down under Section 14B of EPF & MP
Act read with Para 32A of EPF Scheme, Para 5 of EPS-1995 and Para 8A of EDLI
Scheme, 1976. The damages so levied cannot exceed the amount of arrears.

However, an instance was noticed wherein the damages levied exceeded
the amount of arrears. This happend because the damages were calculated by using
erroneous formula through the MS Excel programme. This practice is highly irregular -
and is not acceptable.

It is therefore, advised that the office should be cautious while levying
penal damages against defaulting establishment. Scrupulous implementation and
utilization of CCTS programme for levying of penal damages may be ensured after
verifying relevant returns like chalian, Form 12A, DCBR etc.

Yours faithfully,

Col

Subject: Pendency of DPG and CPGRAMS cases- regarding.
Sir,
Kindly refer to letter no. CSD-IV/CPFC/Circulars/2494-24150 dated
07/09/09 in relation to launching the Grievance Rerdressal Drive in the month
of September'2009. It is commendable that many regions have taken this Drive
seriously and reduced their pendency of grievances substantially during the
drive month. It was expected that field offices would continue with the same
motivation to redress the grievances even after .But it is seen that from
October onwards, flow of rerdressal has become very slow and as a result,
large number of grievances have accumulated in the CPGRAMS .As on date,
total 10127 numbers of grievances are lying pending with the field offices.
Some of the regions are keeping more than 1000 grievances with them. This is
not a very comfortable situation, hence all field offices are ma once again
advised to ensure that pendency of grievances in the CPGRAMS is reduced to
the minimum by 10.12.2009.This may also be noted that ministry is asking for
regular progress report with respect to CPGRAMS.
2. It is also informed to all the Regions that a system of Weekly Review of
EPFO's pending grievances has been established by the Directorate of
Public Grievances, Cabinet Secretariat, on every Friday. So to attend the
Review Meeting one or more Regions, alternatively, will be called to
Delhi with their status report on pending grievances. The concerned
Regions shall be directly answerable to DPG, in case of any ignorance or
non-attendance of grievances properly.

2
Hence, it is advised to all Regions that: -
a) Up to date status in'relation of each and every pending case should be
prepared on daily basis.
b) An officer not below the rank of RPFC-II should be ready for deputation
to the above said Meeting, whenever called by the Directorate of Public
Grievances, Cabinet Secretariat.
c) Special attention should be paid fOr prompt disposal of grievances
referred by VIPs, MOL, PMO, and DPG.
d) In case the grievance does not relate to the forwarded office, the same
should not be returned to the parent office but should be re-forwarded
to the correct office and in no case such grievances would be returned
to DPG or Head office.
e) In case of a grievance involving two or more regions, the responsibility of
final settlement of the grievance rests with:the office from where the
grievance has originated initially. In such cases, it would be responsibility
of the concerned field office to obtain final rerdressal of the grievance
from the other field office and report to DPG/Head office.
f)
All DPG/PMO/LMO/MOL/VIP and CPFC grievances should be reported
to Head Office under signatures _ ,Of Regional Provident Fund
commissioner-I only.
Further you are requested to go through the Minutes of the DPG Meeting
enclosed and comply with the directions mentioned therein. Your action taken
report must reach undersigned by 15.12.2009
You s faithfully,
Encl.: as above.

Sub: Determination of eligible service under Para 9 of EPS, 1995— Rounding off of
Past Service and Actual Service.
Sir,
Attention is invited to this office circular of even number dated 19-2-2009 (copy
encloged)'on the above subject.
As per the instructions contained in the aforesaid circular, all the cases for combined
rounding off of past and actual service referred to Head Office were considered as rejected.
There are many instances where the eligibility is lost by the rounding off of service
although the members would be eligible if their total service (Past + Actual) is considered with
appropriate rounding off. A proposal was referred to the Central Government to amend Para 9
for allowing pensionary benefits for such marginal cases where eligibility is lost due to the
separate rounding off of past service and actual service.
Central Government has approved and notified (GSR — 594(E) dated 21.8.2009) the
amendment and substituted explanation below Para 9 (b) effective from the date of notification.
The said notification has been circulated earlier and also available in EPFO website.
Accordingly aggregate of past service and actual service for less than six months shall be ignored
and six months and above shall be rounded off to a year.
The date of implementation of above amendment would be based on the date of
commencement of pension. To be more clear all monthly member pension cases where date of
commencement of pension is before 21.08.20091member would not be eligible for combined
rounding off of aggregate of actual service and past service.
It is also clarified that while issuing Scheme Certificate the exact past service and actual
service be mentioned without any rounding off.

Sub.: Clarification regarding grant of nominee pension.
Ref.: RPFC Kanpur letter No.390419/CPF/IJP/8/11408/AG-9 dated 25-6-2009.
Sir
The Employees' Pension Scheme 1995 provides for pension to the nominee
under para 16(5)(a) where the member is unmarried or who does not have any living
spouse and / or an eligible child. The said nomination has to be made as provided in
para 61 of EPF Scheme 1952. Pam 61 of EPF Scheme 1952 provides as under:
"A P.F. member shall make in his declaration in Form 2, a nomination conferring
the right to receive the amount in the member's account". The said para 61
provides that the nomination made by member may at any time be modified in
Form 2.
The application form for issuing Scheme Certificate (Form 10C) and for claiming
monthly member pension (10D) as prescribed by Head Office provides the column for
furnishing / updating the nomination by the member. These prescribed Forms are in use
since February 1998 and Pam 4.3.3 of MAP-III supports the practice of modification to
the nomination earlier exercised by the member through application Form i.e. Form
IOC and 10D.
In recent case referred by Regional P.F.Commissioner, Kanpur for guidance, it is
observed that the provisions of MAP-Part-III as detailed above and the practice of
nomination through Form 10C and 10D are contrary to the Law Provisions.
Contd

In order to overcome the situation and to continue the prevailing practice of
nomination, all Regional Offices/Sub Regional Offices are instructed to insist for
nomination in Form 2 (Revised) along with each Form 10C (for issue of Scheme
Certificate) and Form 10D (darning Monthly Member Pension) whenever the nominee
details are furnished by the member against Sl. No.9(6) of Form 10C & SI. No. 12 of
10D. These instructions are to be followed strictly by all concerned..

establishments should be requested to provide the data in softcopy. Subsequently, the
data structure and the software to capture the data were also provided to the field offices

Sir,
A comprehensive compliance audit of all the exempted/relaxed
establishments (u/s 17(1)/ para 79 or para 27A) shall be undertaken by all officerin-charge of ROs/SROs during November and December, 2009. The audit shall

RPFC-II/APFC. It shall be extended to all the establishments that are
exempted/relaxed including those in respect of which the application of
exemption is under process. A proforma (Annexure-I) enclosed herewith should
be duly filled up by the squad after completing the compliance audit and the
same should be submitted to their office for further necessary action.
2)

in a time bound manner by forming sufficient squads to cover all the exempted
establishments under their jurisdiction.
3)

respect of the establishment as well as its P.F. Trust, hence thorough scrutiny of
all the relevant records should be made before recording the observation in the
proforma (Annexure-I).

compliance audit could not be completed as the establishment was participating
in a trust which was located outside the jurisdiction of the concerned RPFC. It is
therefore directed that in such cases either the trust records be called for or the
RPFC in whose jurisdiction the said trust exists should be requested to audit the

Sub: Guidelines for submission of Form for requesting for grant of Subsidy from
Central Administration Account No. 4 to Regional Administration Account
No. 2.

Sir,

On a close review of the existing Proforma requesting for grant of Subsidy by
transfer of amount from Central administration Account No. 4 maintained at the State
Bank of India, Main Branch, New Delhi to Regional Administration Account No. 2
maintained in the Link Branch of the State Bank of India of the respective office, it is seen
that the Proforma varies from office to office and the vital details are not furnished
uniformly in all the requests.

02. The recent experience during the process for release of amounts towards
60% of the CPC arrears has necessitated to issue suitable guidelines in this regard
which are as under:

(01) A Model Copy of the Form for requesting the Subsidy is enclosed. This Form
may be downloaded from the Web Site or get typed afresh and stored in the Desk Top of
the Officer in Charge of Cash Section. Not much modification has been done in the
existing Form and as such necessary corrections may be carried out in the existing Form
and the Revised Form only stored and used henceforth.

(02) Most of the Columns like Bank Code, S.B. A/c. No., Postal Address of the Bank
, Office Name, etc. may be filled up on permanent basis and kept ready. Before sending
the Form, the correctness of the Bank Account No. and Branch Code of the Bank
should be doubly verified to avoid any accidental change or omission while taking the
printout due to sudden power failure error etc.

(03) The request for subsidy for payment of Salary will be entertained from 25"
onwards only. The present practice of some of the offices to send the requisition during
15* week it self for next month salary and sending the copy by Fax every now and then
as a reminder should be avoided. The amount involved in this regard is running in Lakhs
and Crores and as such the amounts will not be allowed to remain idle for a longer period
as the Head Office is monitoring the Funds position on daily basis for timely investment
for earning Interest.

(04) A Separate request for Subsidy towards Salary on actual basis may be sent on
or after 25'". The present practice of seeking subsidy for so many items along with the
Salary which are not urgent and which are not justified should be avoided. The
proposals relating to other items may be sent through a Separate request Form as the
Salary gets top most priority for processing.

(05) The Subsidy requisition Form should be submitted duly Typed only. Handwritten
requests for whatsoever reasons and urgency will not be entertained hereafter as the
feeding of details in the System in the appropriate column and generating a Printout is
now much easier due to modification of the Form as Table and Columns and most of
the columns are not to be revised at all every time.

(06) The Name and Designation of the Officer who is signing the Subsidy Requisition
Form are must as they are accountable for accuracy, justification and proper accounting
in the Cash Book and for tallying the figures furnished in the Balance Sheet and as per
the Bank Statements received and as per the records of this office, as the amounts
involved are in Lakhs and Crores.

(07) In the NFMS Return, now modified from fortnightly to Monthly from October
2009 onwards, there should be only on Debit or Credit entry for the entire day as per the
final position on that day whether Plus or Minus Balance eventhough several transactions
must have taken place.

02. Lastly, it is informed that a minimum of 02 days is expected to receive the transfer
of amount bythe offices even though the requests received for Subsidy upto 02-00 PM
are processed and Fax Advices are sent to the SBI before 3PM on the same day and the
SBI also transfers the amount before 05 PM failing which for any reason by 12 Noon next
day. The requests received after 03 PM are included in the next day’s process. The copy
of the Fax Advice to SBI meant for the RO or SRO or other offices will be transmitted by
Fax and by post only after ensuring that the transfer of amount as proposed is actually
effected as per Advice sent and the position is being monitored Closely in the Morning
and Evening through the Internet Banking System to avoid various problem like double
crediting etc. As such copy of the requisition form should not be sent by Fax again and
again asareminder and this is sheer wastage and this accumulates the paper work
and confuse the situation.

03. Please acknowledge the receipt.
(This issues with the approval of FA & CAQ)

Youys faithfully,

Subject: Payment of pension under EPS’95 through a Joint Bank Account with
spouse only-regarding.
Sir,

This is in reference to Head Office Circular letter of even number dated 18.5.2009

on the above cited subject wherein you were requested to incorporate the revised guidelines in

the

agreement with the disbursing agencies regarding payment of pension under Employees

Pension Scheme 1995 through a joint account with spouse only. The Joint Account of the
pensioner with the spouse could be operated either by ‘Former or Survivor’ or ‘Either or
Survivor’. The credit of Pension to a Joint Account (operated by pensioner with his/her spouse in
whose favour an authorization for family pension exists in the pension payment order) is
permitted on the following terms and conditions:

(a) Once pension has been credited to a pensioner’s bank account, the liability of
the Employees Provident Fund Organization/Bank ceases. No further liability arises, even if
the spouse wrongly draws the amount.

(b) As pension is payable only during the life of a pensioner, his/her death shall be
intimated to the bank at the earliest and in any case within one month of the demise, so that
the bank does not continue crediting monthly pension to the joint account with the spouse,
after the death of the pensioner. If, however, any amount has been wrongly credited to the
joint account, it shall be recoverable from the joint account and/ or any other account held by
the pensioner/spouse either individually or jointly. The legal heirs, successors, executors etc.
shall also be liable to refund any amount, which has been wrongly credited to the joint
account.

(c) The provisions of Chapter 19 of Manual of Accounting Procedure part IV,
regarding payment of arrears of pension shall continue to be applicable to a Joint Account
with the pensioner’s spouse. It is clarified that the said nomination for payment of arrears of
pension shal] have reference to Para 61 of EPF Scheme, 1952, in view of Para 38 of EPS-95.

(d) Joint Account may be opened on optional basis.

(e) Existing pensioners desiring to get their pension credited to a joint account as
indicated above are required to submit an application to the branch bank,( copy of application
format enclosed) from where they are presently drawing pension. This would also be signed
by the pensioners spouse in token of having accepted the terms and conditions specified in
the said application. New pensioners after revised guidelines shall also be required to
complete these formalities.

The existing procedure for pension payment with disbursement agency laid down
in the Manual of Accounting procedure Part-IV, Chapter-8 Para -8.2 is being modified
separately.

It is requested to take up the matter with disbursing agencies for necessary action
and to create awareness among the pensioners about the revised guidelines.

(This issues with the approval of ACC (Pension).

. Yours faithfully,

Subject: New Funds Management System returns.- Instructions for
sending the Monthly Return instead of Fortnightly Return.

Sir,

The New Funds Management System (NFMS) was introduced in the year
,2005 to tap advantage of technological advancements and the field offices were
required to send NFMS Returns on Fortnightly basis. The system has largely
established by now and considering the same Fortnightly Returns are
discontinued with effect from September, 2009.

2. Instead, the field formations will now send NFMS Returns on Monthly
Basis in the prescribed proforma by using the Software in this regard. This
should not be furnished in Excel or hard format. Since the NFMS data is directly
uploaded to the Banking Section Reconciliation Software, the Monthly Return
should mandatorily be sent by 2™ day of the following month at
epfobanking@gmail.com. The Banking Section will reconcile NFMS data with
Central A/c Bank details and anomalies observed will be communicated to
RO/SRO concerned for resolution with the Bankers. All cases of Excess Credit,
Missing Credit, Missing Debit and Erroneous Debit should be duly reconciled on
Monthly Basis under intimation to Banking Section, Head Office. Postponing
these activities till the year-end delays the compilation of Balance Sheet at
Head Office putting us to an awkward situation before the Audit. The Monthly
Totals on transfer of amounts in each account must tally with the amounts

shown in the respective accounts in the Balance Sheet. Hence, all adjustments
and rectifications should be carried out then and there.

3. While sending the Returns, details should be reflected in proper head as
some offices have been sending credit entries as debit entries and vice-versa.
Although, the arrangements under NFMS is to transfer one single entry only at
day end, few offices accounts are debited for each transactions through the
day leading to hundreds of debit entries in a single day. It may be noted that
the HO Reconciliation Software does not accept multiple entries for a single day
and it complicates the reconciliation work. Therefore, all offices are advised to
ensure single entry only for one day.

4. Due to high volume of work and value involved, any laxity in
implementation of NFMS may pose a serious problem and all offices are
requested to monitor closely the effective implementations of above guidelines
in the matter.

Sub: Consolidation of quarterly MIS returns in zonal offices.
Ref: CPFC DO. Letter dated 29.07.2009.

Sir,

I am directed to invite a reference to the Central Provident Fund Commissioner D.O.
letter No.MIS.9(1)97/29906-29915 dated 29.07.2009 addressed to all Addl. CPFCs in the
states regarding consolidation of quarterly MIS returns zone wise and sending them to
Headquarters for further consolidation. It was further informed that a proforma would be sent
by head office for consolidation of data zone wise. In this regard is stated that the proforma
has been emailed to all the zonal Addl. CPFCs on 19.08.2009 and 21.08.2009 at the official
email IDs. It may further be stated that the CPFC had emphasized that the said system was
devised to have a more effective system of reporting which not only ensures data compilation
in the field offices but improves monitoring and evaluation of the performance based on the
data compiled.

2. In order to ensure data that the data is reflected correctly in the returns, the following
guidelines may also be followed while scrutinizing the MIS returns at your end:-

(i) Quarterly reports to have cumulative quarterly data:

For the quarter ending June 2009, the MIS should contain information from April 2009
to June 2009, for quarter ending 30th September 2009, it should contain information
from April 2009 to September 2009 and for quarter ending 31st December 2009, it
should contain information from April 2009 to December 2009.

ii) Data compatibility among individual MIS returns:

a. MIS 101, MIS 103, MIS104 and MIS 127 all indicate the membership as on
close of the quarter. It may be ensured that the membership tallies among all
the MIS and before consolidation this may be cross checked.

b. In MIS 107, the number of establishments added upto the quarter in Part A
should tally both in terms of number of establishments and amount added upto
the quarter in Part B and Part C. The closing balance upto the quarter should

-2tally with the closing balance of current demand and arrear demand in
unexempted sector given in the ABP returns.

c. In MIS 107, the total amount in opening balance in Part A should tally with
opening balance in Part B. In Part C the opening balance in respect of
establishments and the amount under current demand should be NIL.

d. The grand total amount indicated in MIS 108 (Part A) of assessed arrears’
~ should match with the arrears indicated in Part A of MIS 107. The total of Part
A should match with the total of Part B. a

e. The total amount of assessed arrears in MIS 109(Part A) should tally with the
total of both current demand and arrear demand (exempted sector) of ABP
sheet. The total of Part A should match with the total of Part B. The
component of damages in MIS 109 (Part A) should tally with (Part B) of MIS
132.

f. In MIS 116 the total challans filed by police in Court in Part A should tally with
total challans filed by police in Court in Part B.

g. In MIS 129 the total challans filed by police in Court in Part A should tally’ with
total challans filed by police in Court in Part B.

(iii) Data compatibility among MIS returns and ABP returns:

a. The monthly ABP returns give a snap shot of the work areas at the end of. the
month. These reports contain details of membership, claim settlement,
issuance of account slips and the progress of recovery of arrears both current
as well as arrear demand. The figures indicated in MIS 107 (Part A) should
tally with the total indicated in current demand and arrear demand of the ABP
both for Exempted and Unexempted categories.

b. Similarly the amount of current demand in Part C of MIS 107 should equal the
total amount indicated for current demand in ABP sheet unexempted sector.
The difference in Part A & C in MIS 107 should give arrear demand which
should be equal to the total amount indicated for arrear demand in ABP sheet.

c. The figures relating to EPF claims area in MIS 120, 121, 122, 123 and 124
should tally with the total figures given in the ABP sheets. The difference if any
due to representation of data may be clearly explained while sending the
quarterly MIS reports.

d. The amount authorized against each category of claim to be indicated
invariably and not left blank.

2. In this regard it is further stated that the proformae sent for consolidation of the MIS
data zonewise have been designed to’ enable further consolidation at Headquarters.

Subject: Strengthening and streamlining of Public Grievance Handling
System—- LAUNCHING GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL DRIVE.

Sir,
Your attention is invited to various instructions issued on the

above subject by Head Office from time-to-time and specifically to Circular

Nos. CSDIV/CPFC/Circular/2009/7521 dated 07.01.2009,
CSDIV/CPFC/Circular/2009/111245 dated 17.03.2009, CSDIV/CPFC/Circular/2009/107512 dated 18.03.2009, CSDIV/CPFC/Circular/8483 dated 02.07.2009 and CSD-IV/CPFC/Circular/2469
dated 21.07.2009.

2. In order to improve subscribers’ responsiveness, it has been
decided to launch ‘Grievance Redressal Drive’ from 01.09.2009 to
30.09.2009. Hence, all grievances (received from all sources) pending for

more than 30 days have to be redressed during the drive month. Apart

from the Head Office status of redressal of grievance should also be
communicated to the member as well as the authorities from where the

grievance has been forwarded.

33 In addition, there has been large inflow of grievances in the
CPGRAMS. In the months of June and July 2009 itself, about 6000
grievances have been received in the CPGRAMS from the Ministry of Labour
and the DARPG. All these grievances require to be redressed within a
reasonable period of time and this necessitates extra effort on the part of all
field offices. During the Grievance Redressal Drive month all field offices
shall make special effort to redress all grievances, pending for more than 30
days in the CPGRAMS. In future, due care must be taken so that grievances
do not accumulate in the CPGRAMS.

4. All Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioners (Zones) are
directed to personally supervise the Grievance Redressal Drive and submit
their report in the enclosed format by 15"" October 2009.

on faithfully,

Sub:- Allotment of Code Number.

Sir,

Although allotment of Code Number is not a statutory
function, it is essential for identifying the establishments covered
under the Act alongwith its employees for proper accounting of
remittance as well as maintenance of accounts and benefit delivery to
the subscribers. The documentation required for allotment for Code
Number and the methodology has been reviewed from time to time
and guidelines issued. However, in the fast changing background of
Industrial Development, Globalisation, Economic scenario, legal
pronouncements and references from field offices; the issue requires
to be revisited.

Head Office is in receipt of various references from field
offices regarding difficulties faced by them in securing compliance from
establishments which claim to comply at some other place where their
corporate office or another branch or manufacturing unit is located.
Establishments are also referring to Head Office Circular No.
Coord/13(1)05/Allotment of Code No./34878 dt. 18-3-05 and insist for
centralized compliance instead of complying at the local office. In case
of centralised compliance by establishments with more than one unit,
the monitoring of compliance status is reported to be diluted and
inspection becomes difficult.

EPFO is expanding into Sub-Regional Offices and District
Offices in order to provide services at the door step of the subscribers
to the extent possible. Accordingly for improving the service to
subscriber area, securing compliance from the establishment through
the local offices appears to be a better alternative. The feedback
received from the field offices also endorse this view.

However, before issue of revised guidelines, it has been
decided to call for the comments from the field functionaries on the
matter with especial reference to the following situation : -

(i) In case of manufacturing units/factory establishments or
industries where the corporate office is situated at one
place and the factory or manufacturing unit is at another

place.
(ii) For other than factory establishments without
manufacturing activity for €.g. Trading concerns,

Educational Institutes, Shops etc. with branches or
without branches.
(iii) Any other specific situation calling attention.

The comments may be forwarded by 20° August,09
positively. Addl. CPFCs, Zones are also requested to forward their
valuable input.

Subject: Strengthening and streamlining of Public Grievance Handling
System— Openin f rvice centers in Metropolitan

Sir,

Your attention is invited to various instructions issued on the
above subject from Head Office from time to time and specifically
circularnos.CSDIV/CPFC/Circular/2009/7521dt.7.1.09,CSDIV/CPFC/Cir
cular/2009/111245 dt.17.03.09 and CSD-IV/CPFC/ Circular/2009/
107512, dt.183.09.

In keeping with the same spirit; all Regional Offices located in
the metropolitan cities of Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata and Delhi are
required to explore the possibilities of opening of facilitation/Service
centers ( other than the one existing at their offices) in the area where
large number of EPF subscribers are located and is distant from the PF
office. Having Facilitation /Service centers at such places would
obviate the need of the subscribers and Employers to visit the PF office
for obtaining routine queries or work. If required, appropriateness of
the location may be decided in consultation with workers/industries
association.

The facilitation /service centers should be able to provide following
services to the workers and employers in timely and efficient manner.

e Furnishing of status of claim

e Handling of grievances

e Receipt and acknowledgement of grievances.

e Supply of blank form

Receipt of claim forms

Receipt of returns filed by the employers

Provide intimation on pension disbursement

Periodically Bhavishya Nidhi Adalats may be organized at service
centers.

The number of days such service centers would be required to
work in a month; may be decided depending upon the workload. The
said facilitation center should have minimum one computer system
and should be manned by one Dealing Assistant familiar with the rules
and provision of EPF & MP Act and schemes and has required skills to
deal with the public. All information /data related to subscribers’ and
employers query would be required to be updated regularly in the
system; in this context possibility of using DIAM, for transmission of
information / data and to answer queries, may suitably be examined.

Additional Central PF Commissioners (Zones) under whose
jurisdiction the four metropolitan cities falls would personally monitor
the working of such Service Centers along with existing subscribers’
interfaces.

Your action taken report should reach by 10.07.2009.

Yours faithfully,

(K. Chandramouli, )

Sub.: Powers exercised under section 7A of the Act — legal opinion ~ reg.
Sir,

Legal opinion as regards protection provided under the law for officers discharging quasijudicial function as part of their duties obtained from the Legal Advisor, Ministry of Labour &
Employment in the context of an important case under the consideration of the Ministry of Labour
& Employment and forwarded to this office is reproduced hereunder for the guidance of all
concerned officers :-

"\ pseeee Perusal of the provisions of Section 7A reveals that the powers exercised

- under section 7A of the Act are ‘judicial proceedings’ within the meaning of
Section 193 and 228 and for the purpose of 196 of IPC. The same are appealabie
and hence may attract Section 1 of the Judicial Officers Protection Act, 1850
which reads as under :-

"1. Non-liability to suit of officers acting judicially, for official acts done in
good falth, and of officers executing warrants and orders - No judge,
Magistrate, Justice of the Peace, Collector or other person acting judicially
shall be liable to be sued In any Civil Court for any act done or ordered to be
done by him in discharge of his judicial duty, whether or not within the
limits of his jurisdiction:

Provided that he at the time, in good faith, believed himself to have
Jurisdiction to do or order the act compiained of; and no officer of any Court
or other person, bound to execute the lawful warrants or orders of any such
judge, Magistrate, Justice of the Peace, Collector or other person acting
judicially shall be Ilable to be sued in any Civil Court, for the execution of
any warrant or order, which he would be bound to execute, Hf within the
Jurisdiction of the person Issuing the same.”

(authority Joint Secretary, MOL&E D.O. No. $-38016/18/2007-SS.1 dated 12.5.09)

Sub: Holding of the Regional Committee meetings — Regarding.

In continuation of Head Office letter of even number dated 15.06.2009 the undersigned is
further directed to say that the Central Provident Fund Commissioner has expressed concern that the
Regional Committee, EPF meetings are not being convened regularly as per the mandate given in
para 11 of the Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme, 1952 wherein it is clearly stated that the Regional
Committee (constituted / reconstituted under para 4 of the EPF Scheme, 1952 for a state) shall meet
at least twice in each financial year to execute the duty & functions explained in the provisions of the
Scheme.

2. In this context it is further clarified that the term of office of the Chairman and every member
of the Regional Committee is three years from the date on which their appointment is notified in the
official Gazette and after the expiry of the term of the non official members the matter of fresh
nominations is to be taken up with the Labour & Employment Department of the State Government.
However, the meeting of the Regional Committee may be convened regularly with the existing
composition until the appointment of its succeeding members is notified in the official Gazette to
uphold the statutory provisions of holding atleast two meetings in a financial year.

3. The above directions of the Central Provident fund Commissioner and the requirement of
holding regular meetings of the Regional Committee, EPF are conveyed for necessary compliance.

Yours faithfully,

further action.

Sub:- Guidelines for improving Compliance.

Sir,

The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Labour in its 28"
Report on Demand for Grants of Ministry of Labour & Employment for the
year 2008-09 has repeated its earlier observation that Compliance-2001
Programme which expected the establishments to comply suo moto under
the provisions of the Act, did not deliver the desired results. The
Committee strongly recommended that a multi pronged and result
oriented Strategy be devised focusing on routine and regular surveys,
creation of Intelligence Circles for gathering information, launching of
special coverage drive and earmarking of areas to Enforcement Officers
along with all other steps which are considered proper for enhancing the
coverage.

The Organization also drew adverse comments from
Standing Committee of Paniament on Labour & Employment with regard
to evasion of membership. Accordingly, Compliance Validation and
Analysis, 2006 Programme was carried out in respect of 1% of the
covered establishments which revealed large scale evasion.

The observations on compliance issues made by the
Standing Committee of Parliament on Labour were discussed in the
different forums including meeting of Zonal ACCs and RPFCs in-charge of
the regions where a consensus was arrived at for ensuring accountability
in compliance machinery.

Therefore, in accordance with the direction of the
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Labour and suggestions received
from all the field offices including Zonal ACCs, the following instructions
are issued with immediate effect to improve the performance in the area
of compliance: -

1,

e All the Enforcement Officers shall now be vested with clearly
demarcated and designated geographical area, to be decided
by RPFC-I after proper review of the work load of the area
and will publish it for information of employers and
employees.

° Subsequent upon the above arrangement, the Enforcement
Officers shall primarily be assigned for the following work

(i) Survey for coverage: The Enforcement
Officers will be responsible for coverage of
all uncovered establishments in the assigned
area and a certificate to this effect shall be
submitted to the APFCs/RPFCs at the end of
the financial year,

(ii) Inspection of establishments not complying
after initial remittance,

(iii) Post coverage inspection of newly covered
establishments for confirmation of coverage
and compliance,

(iv) Inspection of defaulting establishments in
respect of which 7A cases are pending for
want of assessment report,

(v) Recovery of current and arrear dues : The
Enforcement Officers shall be responsible
for the recovery of all outstanding dues of
the establishments of the area assigned to
them,

(vi) The Enforcement Officer shall also maintain
a Register for monitoring the Marginal
Establishments and shall keep a watch on
such establishments by — conducting
periodical review and inspection,

(vii) The Enforcement Officer shall be
responsible to any work related to
Customer Service/Service delivery to
subscribers assigned to him in addition to
Compliance work.

The above fist is only illustrative and not exhaustive
and RPFC-I may assign any other work as deemed fit.

Sub: Convening of Review Meeting of Regional Provident Fund Commissioners.

Sir,

I am directed to state that the Central Provident Fund Commissioner has directed
to organize the Zonal Conference of Regional Provident Fund Commissioners in the 29
Regions in political states as per the schedule of date and place as per Annexure-I
enclosed. For the review meeting at Delhi the venue would be NATRSS, New Delhi and
the venue of the meeting for other review meetings shall be decided by the RPFC incharge concerned.

2. The zonal conference will be in two parts. In the first part Addl. CPFC of the
political states shall review the performance of the RPFCs In-charge and the SROs under
his jurisdiction on the basis of the performance in the core work areas achieved during the
year 2008-2009. The new business goals and targets would be set for the current financial
year 2009-2010. He will also review the core areas i.e., coverage, recovery, annual
accounts and settlement of claims by means of appropriate returns. A set of proforma in
which performance statistics shall be discussed for review meeting is enclosed at
Annexure-II. The proforma in excel sheet format (.xis file) has been mailed
separately to all Addi. CPFCs and RPFCs in-charge. It may be ensured that the
data is fed in excel sheet proforma only and consolidated for each Region at —
the level of Addi. CPFC of the political states. -

3. Addl. CPFC of the political states would consolidate the performance data Region
wise and send it back duly filled to Headquarters by 1* May 2009 by email at
sanjay.bisht@epfindia.gov.in. Similar report office-wise in each Region would also be
prepared and kept ready for further discussion in the review meeting to be taken by the
CPFC. The Addl. CPFCs would complete their review of the Regions under their
jurisdiction by 5 May 2009 positively. The data received from Addl. CPFCs
would be further consolidated for all the Zones at headquarters for the review
meeting to be taken by the CPFC.

4. In the second part, the performance review shall be taken by the CPFC with his
team of Divisional Heads in which the Addl. CPFC, of. the political states and RPFCs Incharge would also be present. Addi. CPFC, of the political states will apprise the CPFC of
the performance review taken by him and same agenda would be circulated. Based on the
inputs he will make a-presentation to set the business goals in respect of the Region under

-2his jurisdiction corresponding:to the targets achieved as on 31.03.2009. Under each core
areas targets for each quarter in the current year would be spelt out and the time lines for
achieving the targets.

5. The CPFC and his team of officers will review the usual core areas and special
emphasis will be given to the preparedness for the computerization under the new project,
awareness among staff, computer training of staff and the time lines set for various
offices.

6. The agenda for specific discussion would be sent separately.

7. This issues with the approval of the Central Provident Fund Commissioner.

Yours faithfully,

Sirs,

The Central Board of Trustees, Employees’ Provident Fund in its 185th Meeting
held on 10.12.2008 has approved the Revised Estimates for the year 2008-09 and
Budget Estimates for the year 2009-10 and the same has already been approved by
the Central Govt. vide their letter No. G-20025/1/09-SS-I! dated 13.02.2009.

| am directed to communicate the Budget Estimates for the year 2009-10 in
respect of your Region including SROs, as enclosed herewith. Please note that the
booking of Income & Expenditure should be classified clearly in Cash Book for
Account No. 2 and Classified Summary be sent to the Headquarters on due date.
Instructions Issyed on financial discipline on earlier occasions should be followed

strictly.

The expenditure should be properly identified and it must be charged to the
relevant budget head only. The monthly expenditure in each head should be
incurred proportionately to the total budget allotment for the year 2009-10. As per
the provisions of Chapter 5 of General Financial Rules, before sanctioning
expenditure, the competent authority should ensure that adequate budget provision
exists in the particular item. Incurring expenditure beyond the budget allotment is
contrary to the Financial Rules and should not be allowed in any case. In any
particular month, if the expenditure is likely to be exceeded the budgetary limit under
any particular head, then the same should have prior approval of FA&CAO. Any
amount spent over and above the allotment without prior approval as provided in
Para 58 of the EPF Scheme, 1952 will be treated as Incorrectly withdrawn and will be
viewed very seriously. In case of any violation in this regard, officers concerned for
such expenditure would be held responsible and accountable and it will render them
liable for action.

Offices only. If should be ensured that the budget allocations are made by

the erstwhile Regions to the newly created regions adequately by convening
a meeting for this purpose by association of RPFCs of both the Regions.

The element of ‘Dearness Pay’ has been dispensed with, and a new element
of ‘Grade Pay’ has come into force on implementation of 6 Central Pay
Commissions recommendations. Hence, the Budget Head ‘Dearness Pay’ may
be replaced with ‘Grade Pay’. In the current financial year from 1st April 2009
onwards, the ‘Grade Pay’ may be shown separately and the expenditure
may be booked and incurred from ‘Pay & Allowances’. However, while

should be avoided and it will be adversely viewed if adhered to. Further, it

financial propriety and should be avoided at any cost.

Sub: Confirmation of Scheme Certificate with the respective issuing offices.

Sir,

As per the Manual of Accounting Procedure Part-II para 7.4.5 the Scheme
Certificate in the possession of a member is supposed to be received by our office
alongwith Form 5/Form 4(PS) being forwarded by the new employer where he had
joined. Once the same is received by the Accounts Group, they are required to forward
the same to EDP Section through the Pension Section. The Employees Master file kept in
Computer would be updated with reference to the Scheme Certificate received i.e. the
EDP Section would enter the details of the received Scheme Certificate in the WKM
module. The Pension Section will keep the proper records on the issue of Scheme -
Certificate and receipt from other Regional Office/Sub-Regional Office.

In this regard, kindly refer to the format of the Scheme Certificate Control
Register as given in page 159 of MAP Part II. On perusal of the format, it is clear that
this register would be updated every time a Scheme Certificate is issued by an office. In
case the member had joined an establishment which comes under the jurisdiction of the
same office, then the Scheme Certificate received would be the one issued from the same
office and as such it can be easily linked against the original entry. However, if the
member had joined an establishment which falls under the jurisdiction of some other
office, then the Scheme Certificate would be surrendered in the other office along with
Form 5/Form 4(PS). As per point 8 of para 12.2.8 (Functions of pension section) of MAP
Part ITl, the above scheme certificate had to be registered in the computer and an
acknowledgment has to be forwarded to the RO/SRO concerned. On receipt of the
acknowledgement, the RO/SRO who had issued the above Scheme Certificate can
confirm the same by properly entering in their Scheme Certificate Control] Register. On
receipt of the confirmation the Scheme Certificate received would be considered to be
valid and the previous service particulars of the member can be taken on record by
manually entering in the Form-9, Ledger Card, Form 24 etc. as the CEPS Software does
not enable the linking of the captured Scheme Certificate details alongwith the present
service. Whenever a Scheme Certificate or a withdrawal benefit or a PPO is issued
taking the above service also in the IDS, then the details of the same has to be intimated

yo ¥

to the concerned office which had actually issued the Scheme Certificate to appropriately
enter the same in their Scheme Certificate Control Register.

It has come to light that field offices are NOT following the above procedure, as
predominantly one or more Scheme Certificates for the previous spell(s) is/are being
received only at the time of submitting the Claim in Form 10-D as there is a specific
column in Form 10-D at SI.No.15 where the Scheme Certificates in the possession of the
member are required to be listed out. In case the original Scheme Certificates are
enclosed alongwith Form 10-D, then those Scheme Certificates are mostly not being
confirmed with the issued office and the previous service particulars in the Scheme
Certificate are consolidated with the present service at the Accounts Section level in the
IDS and accordingly the pension is sanctioned. Being the case, the Scheme Certificate
issued office would not have any idea as to the fate of the Scheme Certificate issued by
them and it would remain to be open in the Scheme Certificate Control Register.

Moreover, the members are not surrendering the Scheme Certificate at the time of joining
another establishment fearing that it would be misplaced by our office and in turn take
separate Scheme Certificates for the different spells of service and keep with them till
their retirement. But the problem here is, that if the member has died in service, then
there is always a possibility of the widow applying for that many widow pensions to the
respective ROs/SROs who had issued those Scheme Certificates, and as such by
following the procedure of confirmation from the issuing office it can be ensured that
multiple pensions are not sanctioned.

Therefore it has to be ensured that the Scheme Certificate surrendered in one
office hag to be invariably confirmed from the issuing office before taking into account
the previous service particulars for issue of another SC or sanction of withdrawal benefit/
pension to avoid fraudulent overpayments.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Role and Responsibillity of Addl. CPFCs heading the political states in the
restructured set up.

Sir,

Consequent on the restructuring of the regions as recommended by the Sub Committee of
the CBT on XLRI recommendations and as approved by the CBT in its 184 meeting held on
11.11.2008, the Addl. CPFCs have been assigned monitoring and supervisory control over the political
states. Various references have been received in Head Office seeking clarification on the specific role
of the Addl. CPFC in the new set up.

A meeting of Addl. CPFCs and RPFCs Gr. I was convened by CPFC at NATRSS on 19.03.2009
to deliberate upon various issues pertaining to the demarcation of jurisdiction of the Addl. CPFCs of
the political states and the RPFCs in Charge of the regions. The inputs / suggestions received from
the officers have been examined and accordingly, the broad outline of the functional demarcation in
the new set up is as follows :-

ADMINISTRATIVE FUNCTIONS :-

e As envisaged in the report of the Sub Committee, the Addl. CPFC (ACC) will exercise
administrative, monitoring and supervisory control over the political states within his
jurisdiction, and review and monitor the performance of the regions regularly. They will
continue to exercise the Administrative and Financial powers of the Zonal Addl. CPFCs and
discharge the functions of Appellate Authority upto the level of Section Supervisors in their
jurisdiction and as provided in the EPF (CCA) Rules, 1971.

e All the existing Statutory powers Administrative & Financial powers, Disciplinary Powers etc.
would continue to be exercised by the RPFC in Charge of the region within their jurisdiction.
RPFC in charge of the regions will be fully responsible and accountable for all the
Administrative & Business activities of the region and review/monitor the functional work
areas/parameters and improve/achieve the targeted results and _ service’ to
members/stakeholders to the fullest extent.

e To ensure smooth and equitable distribution of resources among the bifurcated regions of the
political state, the Addl. CPFC will continue to exercise the administrative and financial powers
delegated to the Addl. CPFCs of the erstwhile zones. Inter-regional transfers of officials
upto the level of EO/AO within a political state (erstwhile region prior to bifurcation) shall be
effected only with the approval of the Addl. CPFC of the political state. However transfers
within the region will be prerogative of the RPFC of the region, in accordance with the laid
down transfer policy guidelines. Any deviation from the transfer policy would require prior
approval of the Addl. CPFC of the political state.

e Re-deployment of APFCs in administrative exigency within the Region/Political State for a
period less than 3 months on tour basis may be done by Addl. CPFC of the political state
subject to ratification by CPFC.

e In the cadre of SSA, the examinations would be conducted by the Examination Wing of the
Head Office and the dossiers be sent to the ACC of the political state having more than one
region, who will allocate the candidates regionwise against the reported vacancies and
forward the dossiers to the RPFC of the respective region, who will then ensure verification
of antecedents and then issue appointment orders. The RPFC I thus continues to be the
Appointing Authority and Disciplinary Authority upto the level of Section Supervisor, the
Appellate Authority being the Addl. CPFC.

e __ All personnel related issues like seniority list , promotions and probation/confirmation of the
officials upto the level of Section Supervisors to be maintained political state wise by the ACCs
of the political state through the RPFC in charge of erstwhile regions.

e DPC for promotion upto the level of Section Supervisors would be held as per recruitment
rules and the seniormost RPFC Gr. I of the region will act as Chairman for the purpose.

e Proposal for Adhoc promotion to the post of EO/AO will be forwarded by the ACC of the
political State where more than one region is involved.

e The requisite support staff for the Addl. CPFCs would be drawn from the existing staff in the
regions under their jurisdiction as provided in Head Office circular no. HRM II/Addl. CPFC/94/
staff/92/98373 dated 27.02.2006 (copy enclosed) till further instructions.

e All MIS and other time bound returns shall be submitted by the regions directly to the
respective divisions in Head Office, under intimation to their Addl. CPFCs. All correspondence/
proposals seeking clarification on any issue shall be addressed by the RPFCs to their Addl.
CPFC.

e In respect of transfers of EO/AO within the state, Staff Posting Committee with the following
composition is to be constituted under the Chairmanship of ACC of the state.

i. RPFCs in charge of the regions within the state
ii. RPFC/APFC (Administration) of the erstwhile region
ili. Liason officer of the erstwhile region.

e Rotational transfers of section supervisors will be done with the approval of ACC of the State.

BUSINESS ACTIVITIES

e The Addl. CPFCs shail not exercise any original jurisdiction with regard to business
activities and in respect of quasi-judicial powers. However, they shall review the procedure
adopted to ensure optimum performance of the available resources within the region. In
compliance and recovery areas Addi. CPFC shall exercise supervisory and monitoring
jurisdiction and set regionwise targets for improving performances.

CIRCULAR
Sub: ‘Training Calendar “Endeavour” 2009-10

The Training Calendar for the year 2009-10 of NATRSS has been finalized. The Training Calendar
has been modified from previous year’s Training Calendar keeping in view the requirements of the EPFO vis-avis BPR Project for the year based on the suggestions received from senior officers. The salient features of the
Training Calendar are as follows:

1) All the officers will have to get fully familiarized with training capsules for BPR to be able to run
the modules on their own by Sept./Oct. 2009 which is the time-frame by which all offices would
operate fully computerized modules.

2) The functional training courses would be extended to minimum 6 days till October 2009 from
present 2/3 days or 5 days course to make provision for computer training necessarily. The main
purpose of extending the programme to 6 days is that now even APFCs are entitled for Air travel
facility and may therefore stay on Saturday and thereafter get relieved on Sundays to report the
respective offices on Mondays i.e. without wastage of any working day. The second purpose is
that wherever the training programmes are of shorter duration, it would save the repeated traveling
cost and also journey time if such trainings are extended to 6 days instead of bifurcating it into two
different spells of 3 days each. In other words the short courses would be of or 2+3 days or 3+3
days.

3) For 5 days functional courses, on each of the 5 working days there would be compulsory evening
session on Computerisation with sessions on hands on computers with special reference to the
capsules designed for BPR project, which would have a trial run in Karnal on 6.4.09. On the last
day independent run exercises would be checked.

4) Keeping in view the need to improve service delivery to the subscribers and sensitise the officers
on issues relating to Customer Relationship Management one course in each quarter of the
Calendar Year has been proposed.

5) With a view to enhance the skills of officers in Performance Appraisal and Objective Reporting
and Reviewing, a 2-day workshop on ACR has been introduced.

6) Due to the increasing number of cases under the Right to Information Act 2005, a 2-day workshop
on RTI Act 2005 has been introduced.

7) Mid-career training has been introduced for RPFCs-II for 2 weeks and RPFCs-I for 2 weeks for all
the officers having completed minimum 10-15 years of service.

8) Induction courses for DP Quota APFCs have been extended to 3 weeks instead of 2 weeks. The

Induction course for DR Quota would be of 12-14 weeks if the new batch of APFCs comes. A
refresher course for APFCs has also been introduced.

9) The number of courses in the area of Recovery has been increased to 2.

10) The outbound non-functional programmes have been postponed after October 2009. However,
the additional outbound programmes could be taken earlier if functional areas are not stressed.

11) Additional capsules of computerisation programmes would be designed for the
trainers/supervisors/mentors as per BPR requirements from time to time.

The summary of NATRSS Training Calendar “Endeavour” 2009-10 is enclosed for perusal. The same
is uploaded on the NATRSS/EPFO websites www.natrss.gov.in and www.epfindia.nic.in. All officers may
be advised to take note of the above while making travel arrangements for attending the training programmes
at NATRSS.
